language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Welcome to the North Sea. You got here just in time because we are about to explore this underwater city! My name is Lizzie and I am an expert underwater explorer.

Exploring underwater is tricky because it is very dark here. In different areas, we may use different types of flashlights that give the right intensity of light to help us see. For example, if we are in a dark tunnel, we will use something with high light intensity to help us see far ahead. However, when we are in a brighter area, we can use something less intense.

You can think of light intensity as the strength of the light. For example, sunlight has a very high light intensity because it lights up everything during the daytime. A candle only lights up the small area around it, so a candle has a low light intensity.
Let's start our adventure! You will understand more about light intensity as we explore. If we use our flashlights correctly, we may even find treasures!

dialog.text: Phew! We made it to the art gallery.
Can you please help me choose the correct item to use in order to increase or decrease the light intensity, so that I can see the art object clearly?
In case you're confused: lumen and lux are both words used for the intensity of light. Lumen is the total amount of light. Lux is the total amount of light spread over a certain area.

helperSimple.text: Right now, the light for each art piece is measured at 300 lux. Choose the materials which increase or reduce the intensity of light shining on the art work.
